item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Police arrest 14 activists at London protest marking Palestine Action ban
item.description:
Police arrest 14 activists at London protest marking Palestine Action ban

Submitted by Areeb Ullah on Sun, 07/05/2026 - 16:05
Police detain Defend Our Juries campaigners outside New Scotland Yard after handing out leaflets urging police officers to join the proscribed group
Defend Our Juries said thousands have faced charges under the Terrorism Act for opposing the ban on Palestine Action (Reuters)
Off

Police arrested 14 activists in central London on Sunday after they staged a protest marking one year since Palestine Action was banned, inviting officers to join the proscribed group.

Standing outside New Scotland Yard, the headquarters of the Metropolitan Police, activists from Defend Our Juries handed out leaflets urging serving officers to join Palestine Action.

Police arrested the demonstrators under Section 12 of the Terrorism Act, which criminalises inviting support for a proscribed organisation and carries a maximum sentence of 14 years in prison.

The arrests mark an escalation in the policing of the campaign.

At previous Defend Our Juries protests, police largely relied on Section 13 of the Terrorism Act, which makes it an offence to display items or symbols that arouse reasonable suspicion of support for a proscribed organisation, after demonstrators held placards expressing support for Palestine Action.

Among those arrested on Saturday was Reverend Sue Parfitt, an 83-year-old Anglican priest and long-time peace campaigner.

Defend Our Juries said it organised the protest to mark one year since it launched its “Saving Lives is Not Terrorism” campaign, which it says has led to more than 3,500 arrests under terrorism legislation.

“This action marks a substantial escalation in the campaign, Saving Lives is Not Terrorism,” a spokesperson for Defend Our Juries said.

“It may seem tongue-in-cheek to invite the police to join Palestine Action, but the police haven’t seen the funny side. They have arrested everyone under Section 12 of the Terrorism Act. Fourteen years in prison is no joke.”

The spokesperson urged police to investigate the British operations of Elbit Systems, which the group describes as a major supplier of drones to the Israeli military, rather than arrest pro-Palestine protesters.

“The ongoing attempt to silence peaceful opposition to genocide will continue to backfire,” the spokesperson said. “Britain is a country full of decent people, appalled by Israel’s crimes against humanity. The more the Labour government uses repression to mask its complicity, the faster the resistance movement grows.”

The protest continues a year-long campaign in which Defend Our Juries has repeatedly challenged the government’s decision to ban Palestine Action by encouraging supporters to risk arrest in public acts of civil disobedience.

The Metropolitan Police had not responded to a request for comment at the time of publication.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Former UK minister demands reparations from Britain’s ex-colonies
item.description:
Former UK minister demands reparations from Britain’s ex-colonies

Submitted by Elis Gjevori on Sun, 07/05/2026 - 17:52
Suella Braverman said ex-colonies should repay Britain for the empire’s 'investment'
Britain's former Home Secretary Suella Braverman on October 4, 2023. (Oli Scarff/AFP)
Off

Former British Home Secretary Suella Braverman has called for Britain’s former colonies to pay reparations to London for the "investment, effort and contribution" she claims the empire made in building them.

In a post on X, Braverman, a right-wing politician who defected from the Conservative Party to the far-right Reform UK party earlier this year, entered the reparations debate by declaring: “The British Empire did so much good for the world.”

“Of course slavery was abhorrent but to expect the British people of the 21st century to pay for actions that took place in the 18th century has no basis in law," Braverman said.

That claim is false. According to the British government, UK taxpayers were still paying off a £20m loan taken out in 1835 to compensate slave owners after abolition. The sum amounted to about 5 percent of the UK’s GDP at the time. In today’s money, that would be worth more than $3bn.

The UK government admitted in 2018 that it only finished repaying the loan in 2015, meaning British taxpayers spent generations servicing a debt created to compensate slave owners, not the enslaved.

Braverman went further, writing: "If the government is seriously thinking about this then former colonies should pay the British back for the considerable investment, effort and contribution that this country made which laid the foundations for many flourishing democracies today."

She was responding to Labour MP Bell Ribeiro-Addy, who had reposted an article from The Guardian saying Jamaica should "take the case for reparations directly to King Charles" later this year by lodging a formal petition.

The British Empire did so much good for the world.

Of course slavery was abhorrent but to expect the British people of the 21st century to pay for actions that took place in the 18th century has no basis in law.

If the government is seriously thinking about this then former… https://t.co/JWwDtdMEPj

— Suella Braverman (@SuellaBraverman) July 3, 2026

Ribeiro-Addy said it is "getting harder and harder for British institutions to maintain their favoured tactic of simply ignoring calls for repair."

There is no evidence that Britain “invested” in its colonies for the benefit of the colonised. Colonial economies were built to extract resources, labour and wealth for London, not to develop colonised societies on their own terms.

Research by economist Utsa Patnaik, published by Columbia University Press and based on almost two centuries of data, found that Britain looted about $45 trillion from India alone during colonial rule.

At its height, the British Empire covered roughly a quarter of the world’s land surface.

Braverman, who is of Indian heritage and whose parents migrated from former British colonies, immediately drew a backlash online.

"Of course slavery was abhorrent but" is a wild way to start a sentence,” one user wrote.

Another said: “The British empire didn't invest it stole its colonies wealth and resources to benefit the british empire not its colonies.”

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Netanyahu claims Israel protects Christians after Israeli attacks hit churches in Lebanon
item.description:
Netanyahu claims Israel protects Christians after Israeli attacks hit churches in Lebanon

Submitted by Elis Gjevori on Sun, 07/05/2026 - 21:09
The Israeli prime minister claimed Lebanese Christians want Israeli annexation, despite Israel’s attacks on churches and Christian sites
The image shows an Israeli soldier smashing a statue of Jesus on the cross in southern Lebanon. (Screenshot/@ytirawi/X}
Off

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed in an interview with Fox News on Sunday that Christians in Lebanon had asked Israel to “annex” their villages, many of which Israeli forces have damaged or destroyed.

Speaking on the pro-Israel US news outlet with host Jacqui Heinrich on "The Sunday Briefing", Netanyahu said “we…take care of our friends, especially the Christians in the Middle East”.

“Christian villages in Lebanon some of them have actually asked to be annexed to Israel because we protect them against Hezbollah fanatics who want to kill them and we do the same things with Christians everywhere…in the Middle East,” said Netanyahu.

But Netanyahu’s remarks sit uneasily beside Israel’s own record in Lebanon, where its forces have destroyed churches, damaged Christian religious sites and filmed soldiers desecrating Christian symbols.

The Israeli prime minister also made the comments just two weeks after his far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir said "all of Lebanon must burn" in a social media post following the deaths of four Israeli soldiers in occupied southern Lebanon.

Netanyahu, who faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza, offered no evidence that Christian villages in Lebanon had asked for Israeli annexation or protection.

He also offered no evidence that Hezbollah had targeted Christian villages. The Lebanese group’s main Christian ally in Lebanese politics is the Free Patriotic Movement (FPM).

Israel’s Christian problem

Netanyahu’s claim that Christians are calling for Israeli protection also came as Israel faces growing international condemnation for its attacks on Lebanon, including on the country’s Christian communities.

In May, the French organisation L'Oeuvre d'Orient said Israeli troops demolished a convent belonging to the Salvatorian Sisters, a Greek Catholic religious order, in the village of Yaroun.

In April, an image showing an Israeli soldier using a jackhammer to smash a statue of Jesus on a cross in southern Lebanon went viral on social media.

Israeli extremists are terrorising Palestinian Christians and their holy sites
Read More »

Israel’s Chief Rabbinate later refused to condemn the soldier’s destruction of the statue.

Another viral video later showed an Israeli soldier in southern Lebanon desecrating a statue of the Virgin Mary.

Last year, Israel reduced the Melkite Greek Catholic St George Church in the southern Lebanese village of Derdghaya to rubble.

Israel’s attacks have not only targeted Lebanon’s Christian communities. In the occupied Palestinian territories, Jewish settlers have burned Palestinian Christian villages, while violence against Christian clergy and churches has escalated.

The attacks threaten to undermine Israel’s standing among one of its core constituencies in the US: evangelical Christians.

Later in the interview, Netanyahu claimed “it's not only the Christians in Lebanon who ask for our protection. It's the Druze, it's…the Sunni Muslims and quite a few of the Shiite Muslims too”.

He provided no evidence that any of those groups had asked for Israeli protection.

Lebanon’s Health Ministry says Israeli attacks have killed at least 4,304 people and wounded 12,203 others since Israel began its war on the country on 2 March.

Flights continued during Sunday’s ceremony, but Iran’s Civil Aviation Organisation said regular services at Tehran’s Mehrabad International Airport and Imam Khomeini International Airport would be suspended on Monday as public commemorations take place in the capital.

Mehrabad airport is expected to return to normal operations on Tuesday, while Imam Khomeini International Airport will remain closed.

Authorities also said airspace over the northeastern city of Mashhad, along with operations at Shahid Hasheminejad International Airport, would be fully suspended on 9 July during the final burial ceremony.

Flights elsewhere in Iran will continue without restrictions on 7 and 8 July, except for services to Mashhad on the final day of the ceremonies.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] The Gaza genocide has killed liberal Zionism
item.description:
The Gaza genocide has killed liberal Zionism

Submitted by Ussama Makdisi on Wed, 06/24/2026 - 09:57
As Israel's destruction of Gaza horrifies global public opinion, liberal Zionists are struggling to reconcile professed democratic values with a Jewish supremacist state in Palestine
New York Attorney General Letitia James and New York Governor Kathy Hochul march in the Israel Day parade in New York City on 31 May 2026 (Janet Mayer/Cover Images via Reuters)
On

The Gaza genocide has destroyed the remnants of liberal Zionism.

The obliteration practised by Israel in Gaza, the anti-Palestinian pogroms in the West Bank, and the war to ethnically cleanse southern Lebanon - all overseen by overtly fanatical Israeli leaders, several of whom have been indicted by the International Criminal Court - have left liberal Zionists with nowhere to hide.

For decades, liberal Zionists were the confident public face of Israel in the West.

They encapsulated an attitude that attempted to reconcile a professed commitment to liberal values such as equality of citizenship, freedom of speech and assembly, and democratic and constitutional rule with a commitment to an explicitly nationalist project that seeks to build, uphold and defend the idea of a Jewish state in a multi-religious land, despite what such a state has meant over decades for millions of native Muslim and Christian Palestinians facing discrimination and subjugation.

For decades, liberal Zionists have declared that Israel was a tolerant state committed to both being Jewish and democratic.

They were provided enormous rhetorical, moral and political support from liberal western luminaries such as Eleanor Roosevelt, Martin Luther King Jr, Bill Clinton and Barack Obama, and from major liberal western states led by the United States, Great Britain, France and Germany.

But the gap between what Israel is said to have represented as a model of post-Holocaust western redemption and the brutal reality of what it has always entailed for its principal Palestinian victims has become impossible to paper over.

Two ends of the spectrum

At one end of the spectrum, there is now some belated awareness, and even a dim grudging recognition, that after Gaza, something is quite clearly not right with the Zionist project.

The British actress Helen Mirren, who has long championed Israel, acknowledged as much when she admitted that she "grew up in Europe, post Second World War, and the realisation in my parents' generation of what had happened in the Holocaust was so profound, so important.

But while the Democratic party figures stridently condemned Smotrich's Islamophobia, they said nothing about his anti-Palestinianism

"Therefore," she explained, "the creation of Israel was a very important moment, although maybe it was done in completely the wrong way, in the wrong place, I don't know. But something had to happen after the horror."

At the other end of the spectrum, however, the hoary shibboleths of Zionism, and its associated anti-Palestinian rhetorical buttresses such as "Israel's right to exist", still do not even pretend to consider Palestinians, or express any doubt about the creation of the state of Israel in Palestine at the expense of the Palestinians.

Take Democratic party establishment figures - Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer, New York Attorney General Letitia James and New York Governor Kathy Hochul among others - who spoke or marched in the so-called "Israel Day" parade in New York City this May.

It is an annual spectacle of Zionist enthusiasm billed as an "apolitical" expression of positive Jewish national and communal affiliation and identification.

Thousands of marchers were festooned in the flag of a foreign state that has carried out a genocide in Gaza, tolerates pogroms in the West Bank, sexually abuses and rapes Palestinian captives, actively kills journalists and paramedics and destroys entire villages and towns in southern Lebanon.

Schumer, Hochul and James are all nominally liberal and raised at a time in American politics when being Zionist was taken for granted and when the Palestine exception was largely unchallenged.

Seasoned politicians, they subsequently claimed to be, or suggested that they were, shocked that none other than Bezalel Smotrich, Israel's openly racist finance minister, marched at the front of the tawdry parade.

Follow Middle East Eye's live coverage of Israel's genocide in Gaza

But while the Democratic party figures stridently condemned Smotrich's Islamophobia, they said nothing about his anti-Palestinian racism.

Whereas Smotrich openly embraces Jewish supremacy over non-Jewish Palestinians, they act as if Palestinians are invisible and irrelevant to their identification with Israel - much like a white Southerner during the height of Jim Crow segregation and lynching might have insisted that their celebration of "Dixie" had nothing to do with Black Americans at all.

Then along comes the odious Smotrich, like some supercharged Bull Connor, and says out loud and arrogantly what is not meant to be said openly in the metropolitan western centres upon which Israel depends for its subjugation of millions of stateless Palestinian people.

Elegiac Zionism

Not all liberal Zionists are totally oblivious to Palestinian pain and suffering.

Few, in fact, callously revel in expressions of Jewish supremacy and Palestinian suffering as overtly as does Smotrich and his colleague, Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir, who proudly wears an anti-Palestinian lynching noose on his lapel and who recently said that all Lebanon must burn.

In defence of Benjamin Netanyahu
Read More »

A noticeable aspect of late liberal Zionism is its performative claim to recognise Palestinian suffering, and to acknowledge the injustice that Palestinians have endured at the hands of Israel, but nevertheless to insist that the Zionist project in Palestine is still redeemable no matter how many Palestinians are harmed by Israel. Liberal Zionism has become elegiac Zionism.

The founder of the liberal Zionist lobbying organisation J Street, Jeremy Ben-Ami, embodies the prevarication of elegiac Zionism, the idea that things were once ideal and have since been corrupted.

In a recent interview on the popular show Breaking Points, Ben-Ami tried to update the myths of liberal Zionism by saying that Israel has strayed from its founding principles.

He insisted that Israel was a great and necessary project, and attempted to justify Zionism by pointing to the long history of persecution experienced by Jews in Europe, and by suggesting that Israel's early history was filled with promise betrayed by the advent of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Ben-Ami does not discuss the violent, coercive and undemocratic nature of the British Mandate in Palestine that allowed for Zionist colonisation of Palestine.

Whatever the original motives to create a Jewish state - to combat European antisemitism, for example, or to emulate other European racial nationalisms - from its outset in Ottoman Palestine, the Zionist project collided with the reality of history, geography and the presence of the Palestinian people.

The early leaders of the Zionist movement, and their European imperial backers, were open about their conviction in the supremacy of European Jews over non-Jewish Palestinians, and over Arab and Eastern Jews. They were also convinced of the superiority of European civilisation over all others.

A century before Netanyahu, in 1896, the leader of the Zionist movement, Theodor Herzl, famously described a Jewish state in Palestine as "a portion of the rampart of Europe against Asia, an outpost of civilisation as opposed to barbarism".

Chaim Weizmann told his British imperial patron, Arthur Balfour, in 1918 that there could be no democracy in Palestine so long as there was a native Palestinian majority. After describing Palestinians as screaming, duplicitous and back-stabbing, Weizmann insisted that the British occupiers of Palestine must not be guided by the "democratic principle".

The brutal numbers operate against us, for there are five Arabs to one Jew. The influence of the Arab must in fairness be five times greater than the Jewish... The result is that the Jews are practically handed over to the Arabs. This system does not take into account the fact that there is fundamental qualitative difference between Jew and Arab.

In 1923, another Zionist colonist by the name of Vladimir Jabotinsky wrote a revealing essay titled "The Iron Wall", in which he insisted that though the Palestinian natives were culturally "500 years behind us", they would defend their own land.

He therefore advocated crushing Palestinians physically and psychologically.

A century of supremacy

Despite Ben-Ami's suggestion of an antediluvian Zionist moment of innocence, the founders of the new state of Israel ruthlessly expelled hundreds of thousands of indigenous Palestinians and expropriated their lands and properties during and after 1948.

While they encouraged Jewish refugees, settlers and immigrants from around the world to become citizens, they methodically prevented now stateless non-Jewish Palestinian refugees from returning to their own homes.

As historian Shira Robinson has documented in her book Citizen Strangers, they made the surviving and unwanted Palestinian minority second-class citizens, whom they also placed under military rule until 1966.

More than a century after Weizmann's expression of Jewish supremacy over Arabs, and 78 years after the Nakba, Ben-Ami is at pains to appear reasonable before a global public that no longer accepts Zionist expressions of supremacy and racism.

Liberal Zionism has lost ground to more overtly racist Zionists because the latter champion the ugly, cruel reality of what the Zionist project ... has always been for Palestinians

Ben-Ami admits, to be sure, that he is horrified by Israel's carnage in Gaza, Lebanon and the West Bank. He still wants an ethnostate but refuses to be candid about its nature.

He demurs from describing Israel as an "ethnostate", and instead favours describing it as a "homeland of the Jewish people". This verbiage suggests that such a state is reconcilable with Palestinian rights if only a "border" could be created somewhere.

In short, he holds tight to the separatist fantasy that would allow Jews worldwide to continue to emigrate to Israel by virtue of being Jewish, and to enjoy inherently superior rights to most of the land of historic Palestine, which are, by definition, denied to non-Jewish Palestinians exiled from their actual homeland.

Ben-Ami concedes that Palestinians should be granted their own right to return, but not to their original homes or lands or villages as is stipulated by international law and UN resolutions.

Instead, exiled Palestinians should be directed to wherever a lesser, mini-Palestinian state might be created. The "two-state" solution thus becomes not really about providing a Palestinian future as much as functioning as an exculpatory mantra for liberal Zionists to keep holding on to their Zionism, no matter what Israel does.

Liberal Zionism has lost ground to more overtly racist Zionists because the latter champion the ugly, cruel reality of what the Zionist project in Palestine has always been for Palestinians, something liberal Zionists have sought to deny, wish away and deflect.

At the same time, however, global public opinion is horrified by what Israel has done to the Palestinian people. History has caught up with Zionism. Try as its adherents might, there is no putting the liberal Zionist Humpty Dumpty back together again.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Israel raids village in Syria's Quneitra, installs military checkpoint
item.description:
Israel raids village in Syria's Quneitra, installs military checkpoint

Israeli forces reportedly raided an area in Syria's Quneitra countryside on Monday, setting up a military checkpoint.

According to Syria's Alikhbariah TV, troops installed a checkpoint on the main road leading to the village of Saida al-Jolan.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Revealed: landmark Scottish AI project has no prospect of meeting renewables promise
item.description:
Exclusive: Government and developers privately acknowledged Lanarkshire datacentre site had power provision ‘issue’

  • ‘It’s smoke and mirrors’: hope turns to fear in Scottish village chosen for AI datacentre

  • What are Britain’s AI growth zones and are the plans feasible or ‘complete bunk’?

A landmark AI development billed as delivering jobs and prosperity has misrepresented its plans to channel a nuclear reactor’s worth of power to a site in rural Scotland, a Guardian investigation has found.

When it was announced in January, the government promised that an £8.2bn AI datacentre complex in Lanarkshire – built by the US firm CoreWeave and the Scottish company DataVita – would be powered entirely from on-site renewables and built by 2030.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] ‘It’s smoke and mirrors’: hope turns to fear in Scottish village chosen for AI datacentre
item.description:
Suspicions grow in Lanarkshire that local people have been misled on supposed benefits of the huge development

  • Revealed: landmark Scottish AI project has no prospect of meeting renewables promise

  • What are Britain’s AI growth zones and are the plans feasible or ‘complete bunk’?

The promise was that a Scottish community would be transformed by massive investment and empowered to chase “the jobs of the future”. Instead, local people in Lanarkshire fear they may have to sell their properties and lose green belt land because of the errors of a badly planned AI datacentre complex, even as those jobs and investments never arrive.

Late last year, representatives of Oakes Energy Services began to knock on doors in Newarthill, a village east of Glasgow. In letters reviewed by the Guardian, they invited residents to individual meetings. They told them about plans for a solar farm, say local people, and made offers: free solar panels, tree planting, or even cash for their properties.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Big brewers ‘misleading drinkers’ over craft beer credentials, says Camra
item.description:
Campaign group calls on watchdog to investigate sector amid claims of anti-competitive practices elbowing out independents

Big brewers are misleading drinkers about their products’ “craft” credentials and geographical origin, the ale enthusiasts’ club Camra has claimed, as it called on the consumer watchdog to investigate the beer market.

Camra asked the Competition & Markets Authority (CMA) to launch a review of whether small breweries are being unfairly elbowed off the bar by larger rivals’ anti-competitive tactics.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Sky owner announces £1.6bn takeover of ITV’s broadcasting arm
item.description:
US telecom giant Comcast to snap up free-to-air TV channels and streaming platform to create UK’s biggest commercial broadcaster

Sky has announced a long awaited £1.6bn deal to buy ITV’s broadcasting and streaming arm to create the UK’s biggest commercial broadcaster.

Sky, which is owned by the US telecoms company Comcast, will pay £1.2bn in cash initially for ITV’s media and entertainment business, which include its free-to-air TV channels in the UK and ITVX streaming platform. It has agreed to pay a further up to £200m in the second half of 2028, depending on 2027 advertising revenues.
